title: South India set to play a key role in India’s next phase of steel growth: Experts - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
South India is poised to play an important role in India’s next phase of steel growth with an installed crude steel capacity of 46 million tonnes (mt) and production of 31 mt in FY26, according to experts.

Speaking at the inaugural session of the third edition of Future.Steel focusing on South, organised by BigMint and co-hosted by the Telangana Iron & Steel Manufacturers Association (TISMA) held here on Friday, Vivek Nishant Nath, Director (Commercial), NMDC, said the resource availability for production, especially the raw material would be an important factor in supporting future steel production.

KK Maheshwari, President, FTCCI, said there was a need for continued government engagement on policy matters and energy costs, which remain important considerations for steelmakers.

The region has a strong industrial base to build on as India advances towards its 300 mt steel capacity ambition by 2030, he added.

According to a knowledge report titled The Structural Gap: The demand-supply imbalance reshaping South India’s steel market released on the occasion, South India’s role in India’s industrial and steel landscape is coming into focus amid concerns over a demand-supply imbalance that could reshape the region’s steel market,

India’s southern region accounts for more than 30 per cent of the country’s gross domestic product, while India contributes 18.8 per cent of global crude steel output, the report’s cover page States. It also highlights the strategic significance of maritime infrastructure, noting that six of India’s 12 major ports are located along the country’s two coastlines.

The demand-supply imbalance is a structural issue with the potential to reshape the regional market, it added.

Between FY26 and FY30 South India adds 15.08 mt of crude steel capacity which takes the region from 46.22 mt to 61.30 mt, against a national addition of approximately 65 mt. At 23 percent of the national figure, as per the report.
